correctness.rationale: For each ordered pair of distinct maximal-coordinate charts, exact projective spherical Jacobians give the inner product (a+c+sum b_lq_l)/sqrt((1+sum r^2)(1+sum s^2)). Same-index charts cannot contribute below 1/d. Outside a small coordinate box, at least one product pair has one factor >=eta, removing one logarithm and proving O(t^d log^(d-3)) for d>=3. Inside, the exact product density log(eta^2/w) yields the simplex beta integral 1/d! and the eta-sandwich makes spherical factors asymptotically one. d(d-1) ordered charts and orthant area 2^(1-d)pi^(d/2)/Gamma(d/2) yield the asserted exact coefficient. For d=2 the empty-product case is directly exact. The symbolic checker validates the beta and product log integrals, numerical constants, and a deterministic full three-dimensional chart quadrature. Sampling and intrinsic geodesics are correctly normalized; finite checks are not the universal proof.

value.rationale: A positive spherical orthant is a natural regular spherical simplex and a fundamental directional sampling domain for nonnegative vectors. Its maximum two-point distance is attained only along disjoint-support boundary strata. The exact all-dimensional transition from the planar pure power epsilon^2 to epsilon^d log^(d-2) for d>=3, including gamma-function constants, identifies a nonstandard geometric probability singularity; it is not a mere rewrite of the full-sphere angle density or a mean-value calculation. The formula informs quantitative rare-event and sampling thresholds at maximal spherical separation.
